{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script
#
# This is a self-submitting Flux script: run it directly (e.g., `./se_eval.flux.sh <SEGMENT>`).
# It will submit itself to Flux with the translated resource requests.

SEGMENT_ARG="${1:-}"

# Translated resources from OAR:
#   -l host=1/gpu=1/core=2,walltime=01:00:00 -> -N 1 -n 1 -c 2 -g 1 -t 1h
JOBID=$(flux batch -N 1 -n 1 -c 2 -g 1 -t 1h --wrap "bash $0 __flux_inner $SEGMENT_ARG")

echo "Submitted Flux job: $JOBID"

if [ "${1:-}" = "__flux_inner" ]; then
  SEGMENT="${2:?missing SEGMENT argument}"

  # NOTE: OAR -q production not translated.
  # Performance implication: without a queue/constraint mapping, the job may run on any eligible resources; you are not forcing the 'production' queue.

  # NOTE: OAR -p gpu_model!='NO' not translated.
  # Performance implication: without an explicit constraint beyond requesting a GPU (-g 1), the job may land on any GPU type; performance may vary.

  # NOTE: OAR -p cluster='grele' not translated.
  # Performance implication: without a cluster constraint, the job may run on different hardware/network/storage, changing performance.

  # NOTE: OAR -O/-E output/error files with %jobid% not translated.
  # Performance implication: none; operational implication: stdout/stderr handling follows Flux defaults unless configured at submission.

  # Activate conda
  source ~/.bashrc
  conda activate se

  CKPT_PATH="../../pretrained_models/A-VAE/A-VAE.pt"
  ALGO_TYPE="peem"
  DATA_DIR="/srv/storage/talc@storage4.nancy.grid5000.fr/multispeech/corpus/audio_visual/TCD-TIMIT/test_data_NTCD/test_data_5.pkl"
  SAVE_ROOT="./results/"

  flux run -n 1 -c 2 -g 1 \
    python SE_evaluation.py \
      --segment "$SEGMENT" \
      --ckpt_path "$CKPT_PATH" \
      --algo_type "$ALGO_TYPE" \
      --data_dir "$DATA_DIR" \
      --save_root "$SAVE_ROOT"
fi
"
}
